Marcus / Karthik — internal notes (thread for pricing + tech rationale).

Summary recommendation for NovumAI pilot:
- Baseline config: hosted API + Optimize toolkit enabled, workload-aware batching + prefix KV cache enabled per service. Use warm cache with a 15 min TTL for session-like traffic.
- Latency profile: Expect median ~70–90 ms for 128 tokens on hosted with cache warm-up. For predictable 99th percentile <150 ms, recommend Dedicated small-2 nodes (2x A100 equivalent) with pre-warmed KV and pinned model instance(s).
- Quantization: run a small cal/QA eval: 1) baseline full-precision eval on canonical prompts, 2) q8_0 and q4_0 runs. Our experience: q8_0 yields 2–3x cost savings with minimal BLEU/ROUGE delta for many instruction tasks; q4_0 can introduce subtle degeneration on few-shot prompts — acceptable if we include a scoring/regression gate. Suggest we include 2 quantization passes in the pilot scope.
- Costing note: include an "efficiency uplift" credit for month 1 (30% of pilot billable tokens credited back) to hedge initial tuning. For months 2–3 implement a sliding discount: 0–50M tokens = 10% discount, 50–150M = 18% discount, >150M = 25%.

Operational asks to include in SOW: KV warming runbook, failure fallback to smaller model variant, quantization regression test plan, and a 2-hr emergency ops window per week for first month.

I concur with Marcus on 12 consultancy hours included.

Irene
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 27 Jul 2027 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Optimize toolkit: pilot pricing & integration questions

+1 to Irene's plan. A couple technical clarifications to preserve quality while optimizing cost:
- Recommend starting with q8_0 for the Llama-2-70B-variant in the pilot. Run q4_0 only after establishing a baseline and if token cost needs further reduction; include a calibration data set and automatic rollback if perf drops >3% on the eval set.
- Batching: set max batch latency cap at 30 ms to avoid tail amplification for webhooks.
- KV cache: use sharded in-memory KV with a warm-up script we can run during onboarding (I can supply the script).
- Ops clause: add a "fallback model" policy into the SOW that allows auto-failover to a lower-capacity, unquantized variant under load or detected quality regression. That reduces risk and helps procurement accept quantization.

I'll attach the KV warm-up shim and a small measurement plan to the Drive link Marcus shared.

Karthik
Lead Inference Engineer
Redwood Inference
